newsitem.title: PERU: Fujimori confirms Peru jet purchase - state news.
newsitem.headline: Fujimori confirms Peru jet purchase - state news.

text.p: President Alberto Fujimori confirmed Peru has bought a squadron of fighter planes but said the country was not trying to start an arms race with its neighbour Ecuador, state news agency Andina reported on Friday.

"I am not going to speak of numbers nor amounts. This is only a question of us maintaining the balance," Fujimori told reporters in Malaysia on the final leg of a four-country Southeast Asia tour, Andina reported. Peru bought the planes "to replace its weaponry" and "simply recover its operating capacity," he said.

Top military sources said this week Peru had bought 12 Russian-built MiG-29 planes to replace obsolete jets. Peru's military estimates the air force needs a total of 18 new MiG fighters, documents obtained by Reuters said.

Fujimori was in Malaysia on the final leg of a four-nation Southeast Asia tour. The purchase from a former Soviet state whose identity has not been confirmed has been controversial. Peru last year fought a month-long border war with Ecuador in which five Peruvian jets were damaged and is holding peace talks with Quito.

Fujimori said he expected Washington, one of four guarantors of a decades-old peace treaty between Peru and its neighbour, to understand the air force was only replacing old jets. But the U.S. State Department said on Thursday it was disappointed by the Peruvian purchase and urged Peru and Ecuador to avoid an arms race in their border dispute.
Ecuador, which earlier this year bought four Israeli K-Fir combat planes, said the purchase of 12 sophisticated MiG jets by Peru could result in an arms race.

Opposition party sources in Peru said Congress recently approved in secret $350 million for the air force to buy new jets. The sources said Peru bought the MiGs from a former Soviet state whose identity was not clear. It was also unclear when the planes were expected to be delivered.

As part of the peace process, the two Andean nations met this month to try to open up an exchange of information on weapons' purchases. Early in 1995, they fought an undeclared war that left scores dead and hundreds injured on both sides.
The United States, Argentina, Chile and Brazil are the guarantor nations of the 1942 Rio Protocol peace treaty between Peru and Ecuador and have agreed to work for an end to the old border dispute.
